title: I Let the PTA Fundraiser Spreadsheet Show the Missing Cash

parts.text: I opened the cookie-dough sheet and the cash column stopped on Tuesday. I am forty-one, teacher, accidentally the adult in the room. PTA treasurer Brooke handled cash boxes with a smile. Tuesday's fair had been busy. I had watched her tuck bills into a zip pouch. The pouch had a unicorn sticker, ridiculous, memorable. The gym still smelled like popcorn and wet sneakers. Brooke said, "Don't audit volunteers" I said, "Then don't leave Tuesday blank" Brooke said the sheet lagged. The bank deposit lagged more. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The unicorn pouch is gone from the cash box, and Tuesday is a hole in the sheet.

parts.text: I asked the principal's secretary, Elaine, for the deposit log. Tuesday was missing there too. Brooke found the pouch in her car, she said, under a car seat. The bills smelled like the gym, which was at least consistent. She deposited them with Elaine watching. The PTA voted dual control after that, two signatures, boring, correct. Brooke called me suspicious in a group text. Several parents said suspicious is how money stays. I still teach. I still hate popcorn smell. The unicorn sticker peeled and I kept it in a drawer like a weird coin. Elaine said, "I need a second count" Brooke said, "It was in my car" Cookie dough arrived late and too sweet. Kids did not care. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted.
